comments.author: @alexp3620
comments.text:
Every day new SHOCK shocks the shock from the day before. I am shocked.

Let me say what I am thinking about AGI after studying this topic. No, I am not an expert but understand technical part of it as a developer.

1. Current LLMs are more like a snapshot of a brain in time and space. Real brain has to be able to "think". Thinking is changing of it's state all the time. So the real brain is never static. To reach this level of constant self fine-tuning would require huge amount of computing resources.

2. While we represent our thinking in words most of the time, real thinking is not only words. These are visual, audio, feelings inputs that result abstract thinking process in our brain that we don't understand yet. That inner voice in form of words is just our brain trying to structure thoughts and communicate with itself. Current LLMs accept only words input, even if it is an image or audio that we show them are just a sequence of basically words (tokens). So to make it work like a real brain we have to combine different models like stable diffusion, LLM etc into one model. We don't have this technology yet.

My conclusion: while so far we may get highly intelligent model it will not be AGI. It will not be able to understand and to perform all tasks on human level yet. Also it will never have consciousness as LLM. It would require different technology shift and hardware.

comments.text:
Here's a lesson nobody asked for.

Epoch is of Greek origin, derived from Epokhē which loosely translates to a fixed point in time, it was adopted into the English language as epoch (ehPOK), even though the British use EEEpok, and I agree that it sounds better, even the Spanish translation is close to how it's pronounced in English which is época (EH-POkah).

It's essentially a measure that uses the geological time scale, currently we're in the Holocene epoch. An epoch can be millions of years or thousands.

Essentially you're training an AI through many timelines which is probably the sickest sentence I've ever typed out.

comments.text:
About synthetic data & model collapse: If you just ban the EOS token and generate a constant stream of output from an LLM, and then plug that output into a new model as training data, the new model performs worse on every metric. Repeat, and each repetition degrades further.
However, if you intentionally generate textbook-like synthetic data and use that as training material, a new model can achieve performance comparable to the original model with a lower training cost and lower inference cost. There is no evidence that a new model trained on synthetic data can outperform the model that generated the synthetic data.
